Palladius: I say. For I will remember all-divine Paul, who has called the boasts according to law dung and loss, through the surpassing of the knowledge of Christ. And I hear him having written to some: ‘And I say to you that if you should be circumcised, Christ will benefit us nothing.’ (Leviticus 19:5–8)

Cyril: You have spoken uprightly. So then it is sin and pollution, when Christ has been shown, and the time has driven past according to which the law and the prophets were, to hold against the worship as in shadows; and to attempt to bring forward to God a sheep, or fat, or frankincense; though the Son says clearly to God and Father: ‘Sacrifice and offering you did not will, but a body you fitted for me. Whole-burnt-offerings and concerning sin you were not well-pleased, then I said, Behold I have come; in a heading of a book it has been written concerning me, to do, O God, your will.’ (Philippians 3:8) For having dedicated himself as an unblemished victim for us, the Son has set the things in law, not able to take away sins; for end of law and of prophets is Christ (Galatians 5:2) (Hebrews 10:5–7) (Romans 10:4).
Palladius: You have spoken well.
notes_covered: third day / yesterday = old worship after Christ
translator_notes: §26 self-contained dialogue block.

title: Father approachable only through Son; eighth day = resurrection age; milk = immature
english: Cyril: So then through legal worship the Father is unapproachable, after the perfection in Christ, and he is approachable through the Son alone. Therefore also he was saying, ‘No one comes toward the Father, except through me.’ (John 14:6) And that everything not in Christ is both unsacrificed and incomplete, and acceptable and most sacred is the through him and in him, would also become clear through what the law says in the Exodus: ‘You will not boil a lamb in its mother’ (Exodus 23:19)s milk’; and in the Leviticus: ‘And Lord spoke toward Moses saying: A calf or sheep or goat which should be born, will also be seven days under its mother. And on the eighth day and beyond, it will be accepted unto gifts a fruit-offering to the Lord, and a calf and a sheep, it and its child you will not slaughter in one day.’ (Leviticus 22:27–28) So then he does not allow to slaughter a lamb newly-born and still under-breast, showing that the still incomplete and as in understanding short and weak is not yet sacred; and still unacceptable on account of this to God. Such some were both unwise and small-knowing, toward whom all-divine Paul writes: ‘For also owing to be teachers through the time, again you have need of the one teaching you what are the elements of the beginning of the oracles of God, and you have become having need of milk, not of solid food; and the solid food is of perfect ones.’ (Hebrews 5:12–14) So then still incomplete is the in milk and under breast, according at least to the in understanding I mean and spiritual stoutness; and let the word concerning these go for us again, as from a type of the things in sense and clear, upon the things beyond sense and intelligible, yet that all things have come to be in Christ and in perfection and acceptance, you will understand very well. For the animals being brought forward and dedicated to God, he says must be seven days under the mother, and on the eighth day and beyond, will be a gift, and unto a fruit-offering to God.
Palladius: The word is not very clear.
Cyril: Or do you not say that the eighth is the resurrection day of the Savior, and as a beginning of a new age, with the according to law as in the first seven days having ridden past?
Palladius: I say.

Cyril: So then still unsacred and not-to-be-brought-forward is the as in time the according to the law clearly the in fleshly worship; and already a gift and well-acceptable to God is every thing remaining in Christ according to the eighth and beyond. For unceasing is the calling in Christ, having beginning the resurrection. And knowing this the Son himself was saying, sometimes, ‘When I am lifted up from the earth, I will drag all toward myself,’ (John 12:32) and sometimes, ‘Amen I say to you, unless the grain having fallen into the earth should die, it remains alone; and if it should die, it bears more fruit.’ (John 12:24)
Palladius: You have spoken uprightly. And the not needing to be destroyed-together
notes_covered: Exod 23 / Lev 22 milk and eighth day
translator_notes: Ends mid into §28 mother/children one day.

title: Mother not killed with young = Jerusalem spared; no grove by altar = no pagan décor
english: Palladius: …needing mother with the children in one day, what again would it be?

Cyril: Having legislated very well the things upon Christ, and having announced beforehand gracefully the perfection through him, he has not been ignorant, as God, of the unpersuaded of the Jews, and of Jerusalem’s hard-to-rein, and that on account of this cause those from Israel will be destroyed as Lord-killers, and having behaved drunkenly savagely unto the Son, yet Jerusalem will not go away entirely root-and-all, but will remain as desolate of children, awaiting the last and in ends time, according to which she herself also will be saved running behind the nations; for she has been set unto a back—that is, behind—according to the Psalmist’s voice, ‘Because he will set them a back’ (Psalm 21:12); for all Israel will be saved, with the flock from nations having been folded beforehand in the divine pens. So then the law does not allow the corruption as in a last total-destruction to come to be, announcing beforehand the anger upon the unpersuaded mixed with gentleness, and at the same time, I think, setting the matter as some types of necessary knowledge. For least of all will the beings go away unto nothing being tyrannized by unmixed corruption, but this will remain as in successions in that, and that perhaps in this being saved, according at least to the same-race or same-form, God driving away the utter destruction of his own creatures. ‘For he created unto being all things and saving are the begettings of the world,’ (Leviticus 22:28) according to what has been written. And the fore-announcement of such things was also fitting, and indeed also the showing, of the words concerning Christ, through whom and in whom the things corrupted are saved, and what is tyrannized by death has bloomed again unto life, for the root of the human race has died as some mother, as in Adam, yet those from her—that is, we—have bloomed again in Christ and we are and are saved, having him as life and as a second root of the race.
Palladius: How well indeed and very polished the word holds.

Cyril: And it is worthy, O Palladius, to bring upon the things said: ‘You will not plant for yourself a grove; every tree beside the altar of Lord your God, you will not make for yourself, you will not set for yourself a pillar, which Lord your God has hated.’ (Romans 11:26) For see how he wholly houses-out the worshipper of the truth from idol-fitting deceit, least of all allowing to use up the laws of Greeks, and charging that the customs beside those must be shaken off, even if they should have nothing grieving, and if they should perhaps come to be.
Palladius: What sort of thing do you say?

Cyril: Greeks taking all the most well-branching of plants and thickly leafy occupying a thicket were setting altars and sacrifices to the demons. For it was necessary, necessary that as it were a carrying-away of mind, and indeed also worldly delights, have been fixed beside the altars of the demons. For the false is sick from home with the weak, and is often beautified with the imported adornments, (Wisdom 1:14) (Deuteronomy 16:21–22) (Deuteronomy 16:21)
translator_notes: Ends mid into §29 women’s adornment comparison.

title: Truth’s altar needs no pagan cosmetics; princes’ wagons/oxen; Judah’s first gift
english: Cyril: …just as indeed also the unseemly things of the women. And for the divine altar flashing with the beauty of the truth, of what outside helps, or random adornments, was there need? For the divine is not approachable through worldly delight, nor with a mind somehow relaxed and kindling toward the fleshly things, but as in a sober understanding and looking much toward the above and in heavens. If entirely there was also under trunks perhaps, as having come to be from itself somewhere a divine altar, the matter would have wronged nothing the firm and genuine worshipper of the Savior; but since the practice is entirely Greek, the imitation must be declined, and the resembling of the custom, just as indeed, for the faithful and stood mind toward true knowledge, there is no idol in world, nor is there an idol-sacrifice, yet to eat is not allowed, another charging through the conscience of the weaker; ‘For why am I judged by another conscience? If I share by grace, why am I blasphemed, for what I give thanks?’ (1 Corinthians 8:4) So then the matter is well-reputed beside God—I mean to decline the same-working toward Greeks, as both in the setting of the altars, and in the customs and manners concerning religion.
Palladius: I agree.

Cyril: And that one must fruit-bear unto glory of God, and not go into the holy tent having empty hands, the sacred Letter was clarifying again for us, holding thus in the Numbers: ‘And it came to be, on which day Moses finished, so as to raise the tent, and he anointed it, and sanctified it, and all its vessels, and the altar, and all its vessels, and he anointed them, and sanctified them. And the rulers of Israel brought forward, twelve rulers of houses of their families… And they brought their gift opposite Lord, six covered wagons, and twelve oxen, a wagon from two rulers, and a calf from each. And they brought forward opposite the tent. And Lord said toward Moses, saying: Take from them, and they will be toward the liturgical works of the tent of the testimony, and you will give them to the Levites each according to his liturgy.’ (1 Corinthians 10:29–30) And not as far as these were the things from the tribe-rulers; and other things have also been brought forward in addition. For it has been written, ‘And the rulers brought forward unto the inauguration of the altar, on the day on which he anointed it… And Lord said toward Moses: One ruler according to day, a ruler according to day will bring forward their gifts unto the inauguration of the altar. And the one bringing forward on the first day his gift was Naasson son of Aminadab, ruler of the tribe of Judah. And he brought forward his gift, one silver bowl, one hundred thirty its weight; one silver bowl, seventy shekels according to the holy shekel (Numbers 7:1–13) (Numbers 7:1–12).
translator_notes: Ends mid Judah gift inventory into §30.

title: Twelve-day gifts = Christ offered daily; calf/ram/lamb/goat types; Church rests on Christ
english: Cyril: …both full of fine flour having been mixed in oil unto sacrifice, one spoon of ten golds, full of incense, one calf from cattle, one ram, one yearling lamb unto whole-burnt-offering. And one kid from goats concerning sin; and unto a sacrifice of salvation two heifers, five rams, five he-goats, five yearling ewe-lambs. This gift of Naasson son of Aminadab.’ And they were also bringing forward in succession as far as the twelfth, according at least to the equal manner and in indistinguishable ambitions, each one’s specifically arranged day having been distributed; for God was typing thus.
Palladius: And what then is the word of the thus many-formed bringing-forward?

Cyril: So then the matter is fruit-bearing, O Palladius, and a mystical word has also been woven for it, I think, carrying the riddle up unto Emmanuel, and unto us ourselves; and I will speak again as I am able. For when the holy and true tent has been shown in this world—that is, the Church—Christ conspicuous in it many-formedly and all but from us and for us is brought forward as a sacred victim to God and Father, a ransom and exchange of the life of all, one worth-all. For when the Only-begotten has become human as one from us, he has brought himself forward to God and Father, as some firstfruit and firstling of the human nature fragrant in sanctification, existing naturally and essentially, according as he is thought and is God, and again having been mixed in through the human. And being one also himself, he was being written according to many manners, as at least in the bringing-forward of the rulers, and Christ is as it were also now being sacrificed, being thought many-manneredly through the leaders according to times, and having been honored with differing names; and a bringing-forward according to day, the matter hinting the as-it-were unfailing and unceasing of Christ’s sacrifice in every day and the fruit-bearing in it of those justified in faith. For the worshippers will not fail, nor will there be scarcity of gift-bearing; and Christ will be brought forward toward us and for us, being sacrificed mystically in the holy tents. And he himself is our first and exceptional fruit-bearing; for he has brought himself forward unto sacrifice to the Father, and not rather for himself, according to the word holding blamelessly, but for us under yoke and writing of sin. And according to likeness the toward him, we also are sacred victims, dying to world, as sin has been put-to-death in us, and living to God, the life in sanctification and holiness. For these things the bringing-forward of the rulers seems to hint for us, which also examining part by part with the fitting reasonings, how it would hold well for us, do you wish we say according to what is possible?
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then a calf has been brought forward from each; and the wagons, being six in number, have been distributed to the sacred works of the holy tent. Then from (Numbers 7:13–17) (Romans 12:1) (Hebrews 10:12–14) (Romans 6:11) (Hebrews 10:12)
translator_notes: Ends mid into §31 silver vessels / fine flour.

title: Whole-burnt vs salvation offering; silver bowl/cup = Christ as food and drink
english: Cyril: …each one silver bowl, and one cup, and both, he says, full of fine flour having been mixed in oil, one spoon full of incense, one ram, one yearling lamb unto whole-burnt-offering, a he-goat from goats concerning sin; and these the whole-burnt-offerings. And they were also bringing forward unto a sacrifice of salvation, he says, two heifers, five rams, five he-goats, five yearling ewe-lambs.
Palladius: Speak then also before the others, what is between, and what difference one would say of the sacrifice of salvation, and of whole-burnt-offering.

Cyril: Hear then. For the whole-burnt-offerings of the animals were being burned wholly through wholes with sacred and unquenched fire, nothing at all having been excepted, but as it were every portion and limb going up unto a smell of fragrance to God, and the things being slaughtered for the sacrifice of salvation were receiving a partial dedication, as in right shoulder, both head and feet, kidneys and liver, and some other things unto the inward and inwards. So then to be whole-burnt-offered is fitting for Christ; for he is truly wholly holy, fragrant all and sacred. And for us is proper the not entirely holy, and not wholly sacred, for whom there is also something of pollution through the sin in us. ‘For no one is clean from dirt,’ (Psalm 19:12) and ‘Who will understand faults?’ (Matthew 26:23) according to what has been written. On account of this the law has ordered very well that the sacrifice for salvation must be dedicated not whole-burnt, but rather partially. So then, O Palladius, is the word clear for you and sufficient unto easy-learning?
Palladius: And very much.
Cyril: Come then, let us go upon that unto at least saying something upon each of the things brought forward, and indeed also understanding of the necessary things unto benefit.
Palladius: Go then.

Cyril: So then the things from each of the tribe-rulers are one silver bowl and one cup, and both full of fine flour having been mixed with oil. So then the bowl serves the edible things, and is useful unto relish-eating, according as also the Savior himself taught John the genuine disciple being fond-of-inquiring who is the one who will hand him over, ‘The one who dipped,’ (John 6:53) he says, ‘with me the hand in the bowl.’ (Psalm 45:7) And of a cup what would I say the need, with the matter itself crying thus? And a sign of bread is fine flour, because also from it is bread, and bread of life is Christ. So then as in the bowl and in the cup, and as in bread the in both—for they were full of fine flour—as in eating and drinking, life and life-making Christ is signified. ‘For amen,’ he says, ‘I say to you, unless you should eat the flesh of the Son of the human, and drink his blood, you do not have life in yourselves.’ (Job 14:4) And he says the fine flour has been seasoned with oil, the type as it were singing-along somewhere the in Psalms: ‘You have loved righteousness, and hated lawlessness, on account of this God, your God, has anointed you oil
translator_notes: Continues §30; ends mid oil of gladness into §32.

title: Censer = Christ’s own fragrance; calf/ram/lamb/goat; wagons = Church rests on Christ
english: Cyril: …of gladness beside your sharers.’ And a spoon again, shape and form of a censer, having been made equal to a censer, and itself also filled of incense; for fragrance and censer is Christ, not having the fragrant from outside, just as indeed also we ourselves by participation of virtue, and of the sanctification according to piety gaining to be in these, but from home as God and in his own nature being rich with the things through which he is marveled, and he fills all the inhabited world of the beyond-world and beyond-creation smell. For being God by nature and truly, and having obtained the smell of the knowledge of the Father in his own nature, he is known very well, so then the spoon is full of incense. In this way then calf and ram, and indeed also lamb, and he-goat from goats are brought forward, the things still brought forward in addition to these, and through all he himself is being written; in the calf, through the very strong, and because of the animals in gentleness and cleanness, the excelling is the calf, and as in greatness of body, the surpassing; and in the intelligible superiority, all the things of Christ are, and he himself the excelling and lying-above with the incomparable difference according to every one; and in the ram, through the perfect, and indeed through the without-evil, in the lamb; ‘For I,’ he says, ‘as a without-evil lamb being led to be slaughtered, did not know’ (Psalm 45:7); and in the he-goat, through the slaughter for those who have sinned. For a he-goat for sin is the victim, according to the law; and Emmanuel has entered through death for us, and we have been ransomed of the ancient failings, through which slaughter he endured for us. Or do you not say this also is true?
Palladius: How not?

Cyril: And observe that the calves were brought forward, and have been given unto the works of the tent, that in the camp-strikings they themselves bearing upon wagons, might release the sacred-workers from toil and distress. For the Church rests upon Christ, and he himself bears us, not allowing the sacred and honored race, and the people skilled of the holy works, to fall around unto the toils beyond power. So then thus the things named must be brought up upon Christ. And the things unto a sacrifice of salvation the leaders were bringing forward as it were again instead of themselves, dedicating somehow to the holy tent, and bringing up unto a smell of fragrance to God. And heifers were two, rams five, he-goats five, ewe-lambs five. And a calf, Christ, and heifers again we, and a word upon both, not un-akin, but rather true and clear; for somehow always most leadership-holding is the male, and in honor and glory the all-best beside God, and nature is witness, agreeing the matter. And lesser and having been spread-under is the female, and as it were going behind of the males’ strength and glory. So then in a male calf, Christ is our leader, and we have been yoked-under as it were and in much lesser beside him strength and glory, and incomparable is what intervenes. For even if he has become according to us, (Jeremiah 11:19) (Isaiah 53:7) (Numbers 7:3–8)
notes_covered: wagons ease Levites = Christ bears Church
translator_notes: Ends mid into §33 same-form heifer.

title: Heifer same-form as calf, yet Christ far exceeds
english: Cyril: …for a heifer is same-form with the calf, yet in much very
translator_notes: Tiny PG mid-column shard into §34; kept.

title: Christ beyond sons of God; two heifers = two peoples; fivefold flock; silver/flour types
english: Cyril: …superiority are his things. ‘For who will be likened to God among sons of God?’ (Psalm 89:6) for according to us together and beyond us is Christ in superiority of godhead, even if he has become flesh. And two at least are the heifers, unto a type, I think somehow, of the two peoples, having run together unto one the from both, the one for us and with us joining unto the spiritual unity through faith. And rams again and lambs equal-numbered, and he-goats not less, hinting the multitude of those believing, the as in a fifth, I say, time having been brought together, according to which the sojourn of the one saying, ‘When I am lifted up from the earth, I will drag all toward myself.’ (John 12:32) And of those who have believed is signified through the rams the as in prudence perfect, and of the intelligible age—clear that the in Christ—the freshly holding, and through the lambs the as in simplicity and without-evil; ‘Do not,’ he says, ‘brothers, become children in the minds, but in the evil be infant, and in the minds become perfect’ (1 Corinthians 14:20); and through the he-goats for sin, the always needing cleansing and release of faults. Therefore also we have been taught to say in prayers: ‘Release for us the trespasses.’ (Matthew 6:12) For there is not a time, when it is not necessary to cry for those truly fresh-minded, and knowing the weak of the human nature, and, ‘Who will understand faults?’ (Psalm 19:12) and, ‘From my hidden things cleanse me.’ This is a spiritual sacrifice, also concerning salvation of our souls fragrant to God.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: So then I said Christ, as at least in the calf and in the rams, lambs and he-goats, and in the others to be signified, and I would think the word upon this not somehow to miss the fitting. And if someone should choose also to transfer the power of the thoughts upon us ourselves, nothing grieving, to bring upon the things set forth some such contemplation.
Palladius: What sort then do you say?

Cyril: The sacred victims were being brought forward according to the law from all Israel. And the blood of the things being slaughtered was being poured toward the divine altar, all but writing as in a shadow of the thing done, and sideways hinting for us, that we must dedicate our own souls to the holy God.
Palladius: You have spoken well.
Cyril: So then instead of us and for us are the victims, and we are in them the ones being sacred-worked according to type.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: Come then examining uprightly the things as brought forward from all through the hand of the leaders, let us look around at the beauty of the contemplation in spirit. So then the things brought forward were in silver vessels, in a bowl, I say, and cup, oil-soaked fine flour. And a symbol of brightness is
translator_notes: §33 shard continued; ends mid silver into §35.

title: Silver/flour/oil = bright hopeful life; oxen under one yoke = two peoples; meek flock
english: Cyril: …the silver, and of life the fine flour, as begetting of bread of the one holding-together unto life, and of cheerfulness the oil. So then let also from us ourselves be brought forward to the God over all the as in brightness of life cheerful, by the hope in Christ. ‘For with the hope rejoicing,’ (Luke 6:29–30) he says. And how would they not be full of the uppermost gladness, who have practiced very well the conspicuous in life and citizenship of the commands of our Savior? for whom wholly and altogether to come to be in participation of his glory has been treasured beside God. ‘For you died,’ (2 Timothy 2:24) he says, ‘and your life has been hidden with the Christ in God. When the Christ is manifested, our life, then also you with him will be manifested in glory.’ (Romans 12:12) So then the fine flour is oil-soaked. For there is in the life of the saints also the as in hope of glory cheerful, with brightness clearly of the in holiness and righteousness. And a golden spoon full of incense, writing the beauty of the saints, and as in chosen vessels the fragrant in sanctification, then as some gift to God the truly most sweet-smelling. Or would we not think the saints to be bright and choice vessels, O Palladius?
Palladius: Most of all.

Cyril: And a calf was from each, and twelve the all. They bear-burden at least the holy tent, having been brought forward according to two toward one wagon, and under one yoke, and they have been distributed to the ministries of the Levites; and the matter would be a type of the two peoples, no longer having been divided unto unlikeness of dogmas and life, and having been brought together as it were and having run together under at least the one yoke of the Savior enduringly and manfully. ‘For be manly,’ he says, ‘and let your heart be strengthened, and wait for the Lord.’ (Colossians 3:3–4) And an enduring animal is the calf and most strong. Such altogether are those who have chosen piety, holding as a yoke upon themselves the Christ, as being pre-typed in the holy tent. And his body the Church also the divine Paul was naming for us. And it was also said toward Ananias concerning him, I mean Paul: ‘Go, because this one is a vessel of choice for me, to bear my name opposite the nations.’ (Psalm 27:14) And a ram in addition to these, and indeed also a lamb the things brought forward, of both the older having been brought forward and of the new people hinting the arrival toward God and the as-it-were dedication, clear that the spiritual. For just as the enduring and manly was being signified as at least in the calves, according to the equal, I think, this manner also in the sheep the as in meekness fruit-bearing of those justified through faith the in Christ is shown clearly. For meek is the animal, and indeed fruitful. And such are all the exact workers of the Gospel citizenship, to whom also Christ himself has voiced: ‘To everyone asking you give, and from the one taking your things, do not demand, and to the one striking you unto the jaw, turn to him also the other.’ (Acts 9:15) And Paul also writes: ‘And a slave of Lord must not fight, but be gentle
translator_notes: Ends mid into §36 gentle toward all.

title: Goat = confession; altar inauguration; voice above mercy-seat = Father in Son
english: Cyril: …toward all, teaching in meekness those opposing.’ And the needing to follow the things already said beforehand also the bringing-forward of the goat, would show not another, I think, something, except what I said just now, that all need, even if some should be good in habit, the cleansing through repentance and forgetfulness of trespasses. And knowing this the divine David said: ‘If you should watch lawlessnesses, Lord, Lord, who will stand?’ (Psalm 130:3) So then a he-goat is the victim for release, according to the ancient law. And repentance now and asking of forgetfulness is the victim according to us, who approach God in spirit and truth. ‘For say,’ he says, ‘you your sins first, that you may be justified.’ (Isaiah 43:26) And David also sings somewhere: ‘I said, I will confess against me my sin to the Lord, and you have released the impiety of my heart.’ (Psalm 32:5) So then is the word concerning the gift-bearing of the rulers already clear for you?
Palladius: Wholly so.

Cyril: And I think one must also say that, for with the sacrifice from each and as for all already having been brought forward, a beginning of the divine words came to be in the holy tent toward the hierophant Moses. And it has been written thus again in the Numbers: ‘This is the inauguration of the altar, after filling his hands, and after anointing him. When Moses was entering into the tent of the testimony, to speak to him, and he heard the voice of Lord God speaking toward him from above the mercy-seat, which is upon the ark of the testimony, between the two Cherubim, and he was speaking toward him.’ (Numbers 7:89) For when the holy tent has been perfected as it were, and the true sanctuary has been shown to world, which is the Church, then indeed then a voice has come to be toward us of God and Father. ‘For he has spoken to us in Son,’ (Romans 3:25) whom also we say to be a mercy-seat for our sins, according to the Scriptures. And from above the Cherubim the voice; for highest of creation and beyond is God, having the according to every thing that has come to be superiority essential and inherent; and ferrying through unto us the voices from above and from Father, the Son was saying, the true mercy-seat, ‘The sayings which I speak are not mine, but of the one who sent me.’ (Hebrews 1:2) So then from above the mercy-seat the voice has come to be. And you would marvel not moderately examining the approach of the tribe-rulers. For with a day having been allotted to each and specifically, according to which one must fulfill the things arranged and bring forward the gift, they were approaching in order according at least to what seemed good to the lawgiver; yet not according to the order of birth, or according to age, nor mixed and simply poured, but rather having been composed as it were unto a mystical arrangement.
Palladius: And indeed what ever it is which you say, I am not able to think. Speak then clearly for me.
Cyril: Do you wish we say in order and successively those from (John 14:24)
translator_notes: Ends mid Jacob’s sons into §37.

title: Gift order not birth order; Judah first; last first; free before slave-born
english: Cyril: …Jacob who have come to be? For clear would also become and very here the having been altered in the approach.
Palladius: And very much.

Cyril: So then firstborn is Reuben, and upon him Simeon, Levi, and Judah from at least mother Leah. And Bilhah again the servant-girl Dan and Naphtali, and indeed also Zilpah servant-girl of Leah, Gad and Asher, and Leah at least in addition to the other four, bears Issachar and Zebulun; and from Rachel also came to be Joseph and Benjamin. So then first from Leah, the four from free woman, Reuben, and Simeon, Levi and Judah. And from two servant-girls, Bilhah and Zilpah, four, Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher. And others again upon these four; two from Leah, Issachar and Zebulun, and from at least Rachel, Joseph and Benjamin. And one must remember, that into two tribes the Joseph lot has been divided, into both Ephraim and indeed Manasseh, those who have come to be from him.
Palladius: I understand very well the order of the names; and what then remaining is the sought as at least in these, already yours to clarify.

Cyril: Approaching, O Palladius, with the gifts together, they were doing this, not according to age, but first Judah, though being fourth according to time, and ninth after him Issachar, and with them tenth Zebulun. And a company as it were after these second, Reuben the firstborn, and the successive and second, Simeon. And Dan from a slave-woman has also been joined. And in addition to these at least, a third rank through three free, both Ephraim and Manasseh and Benjamin. And a fourth company in last things, of those who have come to be from servant-girls. And three at least these again, Dan and Asher, and Naphtali, though excelling by the time of birth, of those as ordered before in order, both Ephraim, I say, and Manasseh, and Benjamin. So then do you not say the test upon these is necessary?
Palladius: Most of all; what then is the word, try to say for me.

Cyril: A riddle somehow is the matter, just as I myself think again. That the through Christ have first order beside God than those in law; and that the first have been set last, and the last first. For those as in time older and on account of this firstborn—that is, Israel—come behind the nations. And those having the slave spirit, and sons of the Jerusalem that slaves, will yield the excelling in glory to those of the free woman, who is mother of us who have been justified in Christ, and called unto free dignity through free spirit. For see, if it seems good, the exact of the contemplations. For first the tribe of Judah brings forward the gift; from which Christ has sprouted according to flesh. And after this at once both Issachar and Zebulun; and both were free and from free. Then Reuben the first (Matthew 19:30) (Galatians 4:21–31) (Romans 1:3) (Numbers 7:12) (Galatians 4:26)
notes_covered: Judah first = Christ according to flesh
translator_notes: Ends mid Reuben into §38 Israel types.

title: Reuben/Simeon/Gad = hard Israel; free Rachel sons before slave-born; fullness of nations
english: Cyril: …born, and Simeon and Gad, who is from a slave-woman. And through these Israel is signified. And come let us say the upon each, gathering from the prophecy that came to be upon them from Jacob. So then all-divine Jacob said: ‘Reuben my firstborn, you my strength, and beginning of my children, hard to bear and hard stubborn’ (Genesis 49:3–7); and again: ‘Simeon and Levi brothers finished injustice from their choice. Unto their counsel let my soul not enter, and upon their standing let my livers not lean; because in their anger they killed humans, and in their desire they hamstrung a bull. Accursed is their anger, because stubborn, and their wrath, because it has been hardened.’ (Genesis 49:19) And concerning Gad he said again these: ‘A pirate-band will pirate, and he himself will pirate him according to feet.’ (Matthew 23:37) So then in Reuben would reasonably be signified Israel, the firstborn according to time, and hard and stubborn and hubristic; and in at least Simeon, to whom also Levi has been joined, as ready unto bloodshed, and having killed saints; ‘For which,’ he says, ‘of the prophets did your fathers not kill?’ (Luke 20:22) and having hamstrung as it were also a bull, who is Christ. For not alone is the of the Jews caught having dared the darings against the saints and against Christ, and Levi has also run together with these—that is, the sacred race, who sit beside the altar, both Scribes and Pharisees. On account of this, in the prophecies of the forefather Jacob, Levi has also been yoked with Simeon. And in at least Gad, who is from a slave-woman and a pirate-band, as ill-born according to mind, and testing Jesus, and setting snares, unto evils for him; for they were approaching saying, ‘Is it allowed to give taxes to Caesar, or not?’ (Romans 11:25–26) So then—for I will bring the word up again unto the in beginnings—the in time firstborn Israel, the hard and stubborn and hubristic, the ready unto bloodshed, and having accursed wrath, and having killed humans, and having hamstrung a bull, the ill-born and bitter unto tricks, and setting snares and a pirate-band, has been ordered behind those in Christ and free, and if free with us, as in face scarcely to come of God.
Palladius: You have spoken well.

Cyril: And you would learn what I say, also setting the mind upon the successive. For three holding one another were bringing forward successively, from free Rachel, both Ephraim and Manasseh. Then three holding one another and after those the from servant-girls, and I say again, Dan, both Asher and Naphtali. So then you understand that those from free woman enter beforehand and have been honored very much, and those from servant-girls follow at least; or is this not clear, which also all-divine Paul himself writes for us? ‘For when,’ he says, ‘the fullness of the nations should enter, then all Israel will be saved.’
translator_notes: §38 complete on Israel-behind-nations.

title: Camp around tent = circle God; march order mirrors gift order; Judah east first
english: Palladius: You have spoken uprightly; for very thin is the observation.

Cyril: And indeed that the matter has not been falsified, you will know somehow also very easily. For the word also confirms us at once from other thoughts; for in the fitting order God was typing that both the departures, and indeed also seatings, or campings-together of the sons of Israel must be practiced, and he has ordered very well to go in a circle of the tent, according at least to what, I think, is hymned gracefully by blessed David: ‘And I will circle your altar, Lord, to hear me voice of your praise,’ (Psalm 26:6–7) or the, ‘I circled and sacrificed in his tent a sacrifice of shout.’ (Psalm 27:6) And something else is also hinted, the having been ordered to do as in a type. For we must not be put away from God, but as it were near and in a circle appear having stood around, with sin not intervening, with worldly pleasure not distancing us, but with an upright stand of mind gathering unto the spiritual unity and readiness toward every one of the things marveled. For it would be most fitting for those who have chosen to be well-reputed thus that one must fruit-bear. For it has been written that ‘All who circle him will bring gifts.’ (Psalm 76:11) So then he was ordering them to depart-together with the tent, and to walk in a circle, and as in order again, not fitting the ages and going unconfused toward the last from the first, and having been joined thus, and part by part, just as in the bringing-forward of the gifts. And it has been written thus in the Numbers, ‘And Lord spoke toward Moses and Aaron saying: A human holding according to his rank and according to signs according to houses of their families, let the sons of Israel camp opposite Lord, in a circle of the tent of the testimony the sons of Israel will camp.’ (Numbers 2:1–31) Then he shows the place distributed to each; where and how and who are the ones camping. For he adds thus: ‘And the ones camping first, according to easts, a rank of camp of Judah with their power, and the ones camping holding tribe of Issachar, and the ones camping holding tribe of Zebulun.’ (Psalm 26:6) Then he makes mention of a second company and says: ‘A rank of camp of Reuben toward south with their power… and the ones camping holding him, tribe of Simeon, and the ones camping holding him, tribe of Gad.’ And he joins a third at once saying: ‘A rank of camp of Ephraim beside sea with their power, and the ones camping holding tribe of Benjamin.’ And indeed also of a fourth company at once he makes mention saying, ‘A rank of camp of Dan toward north with their power; and the ones camping holding him tribe of Asher, and the ones camping holding him tribe of Naphtali, all the having been visited,’ he says, ‘of the camp of Dan, one hundred fifty-seven thousand and six hundred, last will lift
notes_covered: Judah east / Reuben south / Ephraim west / Dan north
translator_notes: Ends mid last will lift into §40 Amen close.

title: Judah east in light; free before slave-born; Christ-order leads—Amen
english: Cyril: …according to their ranks.’ You see that Judah and those with him have been ordered first, and he has the choice place the toward dawn and south? for in light are those in Christ, and boiling with the spirit. Second Reuben, and those with him. And third again those from free woman. Then after these other three, those from servant-girls, concerning whom has been said the, ‘Last will lift.’ (Numbers 2:9) So then is it not clear and from nowhere doubtful, that the second of the firstborn has been preferred and called-in beforehand—that is, the in Christ, and of those from slavery the free in faith? For these lead through the Christ from Judah; and those come behind scarcely, and have been set as in a second order.
Palladius: Most uprightly have you spoken; and I would praise you of the thus subtle sharpness.
Cyril: To God be the glory unto the ages of the ages, Amen (Numbers 2:31) (Romans 8:15) (Revelation 7:5).
translator_notes: Book 10 CLOSEOUT 40/40; mid-cut from §39 kept; Amen.
